newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends down on importer dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends down on importer dlr demand.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee fell on late commercial demand for dollars, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 57.03 to the dollar after opening at 56.84, a shade up from its previous close of 56.85.
"Late import covering demand for dollars even pushed up the (U.S.) currency to 57.04," said a Sampath Bank dealer.
The rupee got off to a slow start because money rates, which rose early, kept banks busy covering local currency positions, he said.
Overnight call money closed at 22 percent after moving between 18 percent and 26 percent, dealers said.
Money rates remained high due to a big state borrower in the market and investors' squaring up, they said.
"But money will stay high as long there is a big state borrower in the market," said a Bank of Ceylon dealer.
